title: Newton's third law on distinct bodies

authority_basis.claim_scope: Interaction-pair forces are equal and opposite and act on different bodies.

concepts.statement: The two forces in a Newton third-law pair act on two different bodies and therefore never cancel on one body's FBD.
concepts.why_required: Receiver identity is the distinction that separates interaction-pair symmetry from force cancellation on one system.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Action-reaction forces may be placed on the same FBD and incorrectly cancelled.

conditions: Forces evaluated at the same interaction event

model_conditions.condition: The two forces belong to the same interaction and are identified with opposite agent-receiver order.
model_conditions.physical_reason: Newton's third law pairs reciprocal forces from one interaction, not arbitrary equal-and-opposite forces.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: Unrelated forces can be falsely labelled as a third-law pair.

representations.semantic_geometry: Two distinct body nodes carry reciprocal directed interaction arrows, each labelled by agent and receiver.
must_not_imply: the two forces act on the same body
equal-and-opposite forces automatically cancel in every system choice
representations.verification_method: Check that swapping agent and receiver maps one force to the other and that each appears only on its own receiver's FBD.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify one physical interaction between two bodies.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Equal-and-opposite forces from different interactions may be paired incorrectly.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Name each reciprocal force explicitly by agent and receiver.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: The distinct-body nature of the pair can disappear.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Place each partner force on the FBD of its own receiver and never both on one receiver FBD.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: The pair may be cancelled incorrectly within a single-body equation.

required_transformations.description: Map one physical interaction to two reciprocal forces with swapped agent and receiver labels.
Route each partner force to the correct receiver FBD before any force summation.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: Action and reaction cancel because they are equal and opposite.
misconceptions.why_plausible: The vector equation shows equal magnitude and opposite direction, which resembles cancellation when receiver identity is ignored.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: The table-on-book force acts on the book while the book-on-table force acts on the table; they cannot cancel in the book's single-body FBD.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Use two body nodes and separate receiver-labelled arrows rather than one unlabeled force pair.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: They act on different receivers; cancellation is meaningful only after selecting a common system containing both bodies.
misconceptions.verification: Check that each pair member appears on a different receiver's FBD.

problem_families.name: Identify a Newton third-law pair
problem_families.first_technical_move: Name both forces by agent and receiver for the same interaction.
fatal_errors: pairing forces on the same body

problem_families.name: Contact interaction force pairs
problem_families.first_technical_move: Identify the two receivers and write the contact force on each separately.
fatal_errors: placing both partner forces on one FBD

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Remove distinct-body semantics from Newton third law.
